skill.name: lint-fixer
skill.description: Runs the project lint workflow, helps resolve Biome, oxlint, TypeScript, and secretlint issues, and verifies fixes with lint and tests.
skill.summary: Fixes lint issues while preserving behavior and verifying changes with lint and test runs.
skill.author: yamadashy

security_audit.summary: The skill is a straightforward lint repair workflow with no prompt injection, network access, credential access, or data exfiltration intent found. Several static findings are valid because the skill directs an agent to run npm and linter commands, including auto-fix and test scripts that can execute project-defined code. The remaining findings are inline configuration file names and are false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Ask agents to inspect package.json scripts and get confirmation before running npm run lint or npm run test in untrusted repositories.
Require review of Biome and oxlint changes before continuing, and keep lint fixes limited to formatting or rule compliance.
Prefer existing project tools and avoid installing or executing new binaries while repairing lint issues.

static_findings.snippet: `npm run lint` runs 4 tools in sequence:
1. Run `npm run lint` to identify issues
4. Run `npm run lint` again to verify
5. Run `npm run test` to ensure no breakage
- `biome.json` - Formatting rules (2 spaces, 120 chars, single quotes)

finding_verdicts.reason: The skill describes running npm run lint, which executes project-defined npm script logic. This is expected for lint repair, but it can run arbitrary code from the target repository.
The Biome command is a hardcoded formatter and linter command with write behavior. It is legitimate, but it executes a workspace tool and can modify repository files.
The oxlint command is a hardcoded linter command with automatic fixes. It is legitimate, but it executes a workspace tool and can modify repository files.
The tsgo command is a hardcoded TypeScript check with no emit. It still executes a workspace tool, so it remains an external command risk in untrusted projects.
The workflow instructs the agent to run npm run lint to identify issues. NPM scripts can execute project-controlled code, so this is a real but expected risk.
The workflow instructs the agent to rerun npm run lint for verification. Repeated npm script execution has the same project-controlled command risk.
The workflow instructs the agent to run npm run test. Test scripts are project-defined and may execute arbitrary code, even when used for normal validation.
The line references biome.json as a configuration file name. It does not instruct command execution or create a shell execution path.
The line references .oxlintrc.json as a configuration file name. It is documentation text, not an executable command.
The line references .secretlintrc.json as a configuration file name. It does not direct the agent to run a command.

content.value_statement: Lint failures slow reviews and hide real defects. This skill runs lint checks, guides safe fixes, and verifies behavior with tests.
actual_capabilities: Runs the project lint workflow through npm run lint.
Uses Biome, oxlint, tsgo, and secretlint as the documented lint tools.
Separates type errors, style errors, and secret detection findings.
Applies safe formatting and lint auto-fixes where the tools support them.
Reruns lint and test commands to verify the final result.
limitations: Requires a project with npm lint and test scripts.
TypeScript type errors still need manual reasoning and code changes.
Auto-fix tools can modify many files, so review is required.
Secret detection depends on the project secretlint configuration.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Fix formatting, lint, and type-check failures before a pull request is ready for review.

use_cases.title: Maintain Code Standards
use_cases.description: Apply documented project lint rules consistently across TypeScript and JavaScript files.

use_cases.title: Validate Generated Changes
use_cases.description: Run lint and test checks after code generation to catch style, type, and secret issues.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Current Lint Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a local project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the lint-fixer workflow on this repository. Fix lint errors, preserve behavior, and tell me what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Review Lint Categories
prompt_templates.scenario: Separate automatic fixes from manual fixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the lint checks, group failures by tool, and fix only the issues that are safe to change automatically.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Type And Style Issues
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle mixed Biome, oxlint, and TypeScript failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the lint-fixer workflow to resolve style issues first, then address TypeScript errors without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Verify A Release Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint and tests, inspect npm scripts before execution, fix failures, and summarize any remaining risk or manual follow-up.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript project fails lint after formatting changes.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs the lint workflow, applies safe formatting fixes, reruns lint, and reports that tests pass.

output_examples.input: A pull request has both style errors and type errors.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates automatic style fixes from manual type fixes, updates the code, and explains the remaining decisions.

output_examples.input: A repository reports a possible secret during linting.
output_examples.output: The assistant stops normal lint repair, highlights the secret warning, and recommends rotating or removing the exposed value.

best_practices: Inspect package scripts before running lint or test commands in unfamiliar repositories.
Review every auto-fix diff before considering the lint repair complete.
Keep fixes focused on lint compliance and avoid unrelated refactors.
anti_patterns: Do not run npm scripts from untrusted repositories without confirmation.
Do not hide type errors by weakening types or disabling rules without approval.
Do not continue normal lint repair when secretlint reports exposed credentials.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It uses the project lint workflow and the documented tools Biome, oxlint, tsgo, and secretlint.

faq.question: Can it change source files?
faq.answer: Yes. Biome and oxlint can apply automatic fixes, so all diffs should be reviewed.

faq.question: Does it fix TypeScript errors automatically?
faq.answer: It can help resolve them, but type errors usually require manual reasoning about program behavior.

faq.question: Does it detect secrets?
faq.answer: It follows the documented secretlint step, which depends on the repository secretlint rules.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. NPM scripts and workspace binaries can execute code controlled by the repository.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
